chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:

I prayed Maghrib behind Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام at al-Muzdalifah. Then he stood and prayed Maghrib, then prayed the later ʿIshāʾ, and he did not perform any rakʿah between them. Then I prayed behind him a year after that, and when he had prayed Maghrib, he stood and performed four rakʿahs of supererogatory prayer.

So there is no contradiction between the two actions, nor between it and the earlier reports, because the earlier reports are interpreted as recommendation and desirability rather than obligation and requirement, while this action is interpreted as indicating permissibility.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: desirability or recommended status in legal usage
key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the ʿIshāʾ prayer, mentioned here as the later night prayer
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib prayer performed after sunset
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: Muzdalifah, the sacred location where pilgrims combine prayers during hajj

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray a supererogatory prayer between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at al-Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This report concerns the manner of combining Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at al-Muzdalifah during hajj. It shows that both leaving the supererogatory prayer between them and performing it are acceptable, with the reconciliation being that such prayer is recommended, not obligatory, and omission indicates permissibility.
